paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2015 - Boosting Mobile Apps under Imbalanced Sensing Data
title: Boosting Mobile Apps under Imbalanced Sensing Data
motivation: Mobile sensing apps generate massive data but interesting events are rare, making traditional classifiers fail to detect positives (low recall).
problem_framing: Imbalanced classification in mobile sensing where positive (interesting) class is severely underrepresented; labeled data expensive, unlabeled also imbalanced.
key_insight: Bridge under-sampling and semi-supervised learning via similarity-based sampling to use both techniques simultaneously.
method_signature: SLIM: under-sampling negative class + similarity-based pseudo-labeling of unlabeled data + SVM ensemble per sensor dimension.
evaluation_criteria: F-Measure as primary metric for imbalanced data (balances precision and recall); also accuracy, precision, recall.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Semi-supervised S3VM can perform worse than imbalanced-only models because unlabeled data 'may enhance the distribution skew so severely that it has canceled the benefit.'
evidence_for_taste: accuracy of 90 percent is obviously unacceptable
less than half of the positive instances are correctly recognized
it is not as straightforward as it seems
unlabelled data may result in helping a little, or even jeopardizing
both techniques separately will not suffice
thinking_moves: 从实验数据揭示精度/召回率的背离现象反推问题本质
将 unlabeled data 的使用困难归因于其自身也是 imbalanced
把两种独立方法(under-sampling + semi-supervised)通过 similarity sampling 桥接起来
用 pilot experiment 验证 baseline 方法在 recall 上的缺陷再提出新框架
用 accuracy 和 F-Measure 的对比揭示单一指标的误导性
